sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].

FY2017 was the first break: revenue rose 104.0% to $824.9 million [F2][D36], but the net loss widened to $3,445.1 million [F32] on a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the IPO-related RSU and CEO award [P74].

Growth then decelerated sharply, from 64.2% in FY2021 to 11.8% in FY2022 and 0.1% in FY2023 [D218][D263][D311], and the FY2022 net loss widened to $1,429.7 million [F37] as cost of revenue and operating expenses rose [P42].
The last two years re-accelerated to 16.4% and 10.6% growth [D358][D406], while the operating loss narrowed from $1,398.4 million in FY2023 to $532.2 million in FY2025 [F18][F20].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue [D456], contributing 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D458][D406].
Rest of world contributed 3.7pp and Europe 2.5pp in FY2025 [D499][D524], lifting rest of world to 23.0% of revenue [D497].
Advertising revenue grew 5.8% and contributed 5.3pp in FY2025 [D537][D538], driven by roughly 17% more impressions, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression [P24].
Other revenue grew 62.9% and contributed 5.4pp [D544][D545], predominantly on higher subscription revenue from subscriber growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so revenue grew 5.5pp faster than operating costs [D423][D406][D430], and the incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D429].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% in FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The 5.7pp improvement in FY2025 came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp), R&D (+1.3pp) and other lines (+3.3pp) [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising investment [P22], and R&D rose $101.9 million on product development and headcount [P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin [F50][F30][D591], helped by $68.9 million of other income [X130].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million in FY2025 was 1.4x the $460.5 million net loss [F80][F40], and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F100][D393].
Operating cash flow rose from $413.5 million in FY2024 [F79], driven by non-cash stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and D&A of $163.6 million [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [F90][D392][D395], and free cash flow margin has climbed from a -167.5% low in FY2016 [D559].
Cash generation now exceeds the accounting loss, but it rests heavily on $1,016.8 million of non-cash stock-based compensation [X90].
The company moved to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, or net cash of -10.1% of revenue [D399][D400], from net cash of $1,439.8 million in FY2021 [D211].
That ranks at the 0th percentile against an internet peer median of 45.0% net cash of revenue (n=5) [D578][D579].
Total debt fell 2.9% to $3,536.8 million [D398][D427] as $1.4 billion of notes were repurchased and $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes issued [P1][P2].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow [D401][D402], while the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last 10 years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing, but a decade without profit leaves little evidence the model earns its cost of capital [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last 9 years [R2][D390].
At $1,016.8 million it is nearly twice the operating loss [X90][F20], so reported progress depends on paying employees in stock.
Net cash fell for four straight years into net debt in FY2025 [R3][D211][D256][D304][D351][D399], and buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Returning more cash than is generated while the balance sheet slips into net debt narrows the cushion for a downturn [R3][R4].
Whether the operating margin holds above the -9.0% FY2025 high [F30][D554], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether free cash flow margin stays above the 7.4% FY2025 level [D393][D560], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether net cash of revenue recovers from -10.1% in FY2025 [D400], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
